canonicalReview.reconciliationSummary: Two reviewers reached different outcomes (revise vs. block) primarily over whether documented accepted-risk deviations should block epic closeout. Reviewer-1 (claude-code) treated Story 1's accepted-risk deviations (reload using cwd-most-recent, --resume failing closed for multiple candidates) as resolved via impl-lead ruling, surfacing only EF-001 as non-blocking. Reviewer-2 (codex) correctly identified that these are material departures from the literal AC contract (EV-002, EV-003) and that corpus fixtures are synthetic stand-ins rather than recorded PI corpora (EV-001). All three findings are supported by code evidence: index.ts lines 192-200 (defaultSelectThread returns null for multiple candidates), thread-resolution.ts lines 141-147 (reload uses cwd-most-recent), and replay.ts lines 36-38 (synthetic stand-in data). The team implementation log records these as approved accepted-risk deviations due to PI v0.79.2 API constraints and M0 dependency status. Both reviewers agreed gates pass (142 tests, 20 files). The canonical review confirms all three findings remain supported but recommends non-blocking given documented approvals and upstream requests.

blockingFindings.title: Production --resume does not resolve operator selection for multiple cwd threads
blockingFindings.evidence: epic.md AC-1.7 requires --resume to list cwd threads and resolve operator's selection. packages/pi-lhc/src/index.ts:192-200 (defaultSelectThread) presents candidates via ctx.ui.notify but returns null for multiple candidates, directing operator to relaunch with --session. Team impl-log records as accepted-risk due to PI v0.79.2 lacking interactive input/selection API; upstream request filed.

blockingFindings.title: Reload can attach wrong thread because it uses cwd-most-recent instead of resolved threadId
blockingFindings.evidence: epic.md AC-1.5 requires reload to reconstruct from durable state (resolved thread id). packages/pi-lhc/src/lifecycle/thread-resolution.ts:141-147 (resolveReloadThread) returns cwd-most-recent for no-flag and --resume reloads. Test TC-1.5 (thread-resolution.test.ts:336-373) proves correct only when no newer cwd thread exists. Team impl-log records as accepted-risk; design forbids PI-session→thread mapping and PI lacks extension API for exact thread recovery.

crossStoryFindings: Stories 2, 4, 5, and 6 are broadly coherent: capture, turn derivation, fork replay, inference routing, and startup validation are wired through connector entry points and real LHC surfaces.

Story 1 still has accepted-risk behavior that does not satisfy the literal epic contract: reload reattaches by cwd-most-recent for no-flag/resume launches, and production --resume cannot resolve an operator selection when more than one cwd thread exists.

Story 3 does not meet the epic-level verification contract because the corpus fixtures are small handcrafted AgentMessage jsonl files, not recorded PI corpora with the real hook/lifecycle surface the epic requires.
architectureFindings: The observe-only boundary is preserved: packages/pi-lhc/src/index.ts registers no context hook, and capture does not alter what PI sends to the model.
The converter module shape matches the tech design: map-message is pure, turn-accumulator owns LHC turn close, and converter writes through intakeStream.messageEvents.

Reload behavior drifts from AC-1.5 and tech-design.md: the design says reload reconstructs from durable state, specifically the resolved thread id, while packages/pi-lhc/src/lifecycle/thread-resolution.ts falls back to cwd-most-recent for no-flag and --resume reloads.

The --resume production path has a picker abstraction, but the default selector only notifies and returns null for multiple candidates, so the production path does not resolve the operator's selection required by AC-1.7.
A recorded-risk note exists in docs/specs/02-pi-lhc/01-connector-core/team-impl-log.md, but the epic and tech design were not updated to narrow AC-1.5, AC-1.7, or AC-6.1.
epicCoverageAssessment: Flow 1 is incomplete against the written contract: new/continue/session resolution exists, but reload exact-thread reconstruction and production resume selection are not fully implemented.
Flow 2 is covered by source and tests: ordered message mapping, turn derivation, runtime notes, idempotency, capture gaps, parallel tools, errors, and aborts are implemented.
Flow 3 is implemented with replay seeding and derived-form requeue; source thread immutability is covered.

Flow 4 is implemented through createModelCall over PI modelRegistry plus pi-ai dynamic import, with failure classification and closed-loop persisted outcomes covered by tests using injected completion/model-call boundaries.
Flow 5 is implemented: assignments load defaults/overrides, startup validation reports unreachable lanes, and capture continues.
Flow 6 is incomplete: replay is deterministic and compares durable read-back, but it does not consume real recorded PI corpora as required by AC-6.1.
productionPathFindings: No fake adapter was found in src capture/fork/inspect paths: capture uses real LHC intakeStream, fork replay uses intakeStream.messageEvents, and inspect reads real LHC surfaces.

createModelCall does not fabricate output when pi-ai is unavailable; it returns a classified failure.

blockingFindings.title: Production --resume does not resolve operator selection for multiple cwd threads
blockingFindings.evidence: epic.md:141 requires --resume to list cwd threads and resolve the operator's selection. packages/pi-lhc/src/index.ts:192-200 notifies the candidate list but returns a thread only when there is exactly one candidate; packages/pi-lhc/test/lifecycle/thread-resolution.test.ts:255-292 asserts this fail-closed production behavior instead of a selected thread.

blockingFindings.title: Reload can attach the wrong thread because it uses cwd-most-recent instead of the resolved threadId
blockingFindings.evidence: epic.md:137 requires reload to reconstruct from durable state, the resolved thread id, and continue on the same thread. packages/pi-lhc/src/lifecycle/thread-resolution.ts:141-147 lists cwd threads and returns the last row for no-flag/--resume reloads. This only proves correct when no newer cwd thread exists, which is the narrow scenario covered by packages/pi-lhc/test/lifecycle/thread-resolution.test.ts:336-373.
